test_cases.test_name: Temperature Monitoring Accuracy and Alarm Functionality Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that the EMS accurately monitors temperature within specified range and generates alarms when deviations exceed ±2°C from setpoint

test_steps.action: Set temperature setpoint to 5°C and configure alarm limits to ±2°C from setpoint
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts configuration and confirms alarm limits are set to 3°C and 7°C

test_steps.action: Introduce temperature deviation to 7.5°C using calibrated temperature source and monitor for 10 minutes
test_steps.expected_result: System generates high temperature alarm within 30 seconds of reaching 7.5°C

test_steps.action: Return temperature to setpoint and verify alarm clears automatically
test_steps.expected_result: Alarm clears within 30 seconds of temperature returning to within acceptable range

acceptance_criteria: Temperature readings accurate within ±0.5°C
Alarms generated within 30 seconds of deviation
Alarms clear automatically when parameters return to normal
All events recorded in audit trail
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail requirements
GMP requirements for environmental monitoring
data_integrity_requirements: All temperature readings must be time-stamped and stored
Alarm events must be recorded in audit trail with user/system identification
Data must be protected from modification

test_cases.test_name: Data Storage and Retention Capability Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that the EMS properly stores monitoring data in vendor database format and supports required retention period
prerequisites: System running for at least 24 hours with test data

test_steps.action: Generate 48 hours of continuous temperature monitoring data at 5-minute intervals
test_steps.expected_result: System records all data points without gaps or missing records in vendor database format

test_steps.action: Execute vendor's archival feature to archive 30 days of test data
test_steps.expected_result: Data successfully archived with verification of integrity and accessibility

test_steps.action: Calculate storage requirements for 10 years of data based on current data generation rate
test_steps.expected_result: Calculated storage requirement is within system's stated capacity with adequate margin

acceptance_criteria: All data recorded at specified 5-minute intervals
Data stored in vendor's standard database format without modification
Archival feature functions correctly
Storage capacity supports minimum 10 years of data
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements
Data retention requirements for pharmaceutical products
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be complete and accurate
Records must be protected from alteration or deletion
Archive process must maintain data integrity
Storage capacity must meet regulatory requirements

test_cases.test_name: System Integration and Alarm Notification Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that the EMS properly integrates with the facility management system and paging system for alarm notifications
prerequisites: EMS system fully installed and operational
Facility management system available and configured
Site paging system accessible for testing
Test user accounts with appropriate permissions

test_steps.action: Configure EMS to send alarm notifications to facility management system using standard protocols
test_steps.expected_result: Configuration successful with confirmation message displayed

test_steps.action: Simulate a temperature deviation exceeding ±2°C from setpoint to trigger alarm
test_steps.expected_result: Alarm condition detected and logged in EMS system

test_steps.action: Verify alarm notification is received by facility management system within 30 seconds
test_steps.expected_result: Alarm notification appears in facility management system interface

test_steps.action: Confirm paging system integration by checking for alarm notification via vendor API
test_steps.expected_result: Paging system receives and displays alarm notification

acceptance_criteria: All alarm notifications are transmitted to facility management system within 30 seconds
Paging system receives alarm notifications via vendor API without errors
Integration maintains data integrity during transmission
System responds to alarm conditions as specified in URS-EMS-015
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records and signatures
EU Annex 11 for computerized systems
FDA guidance on data integrity and system integration
data_integrity_requirements: Alarm data must maintain accuracy during transmission
Audit trail must record all integration events
Data must not be altered during system interface processes
urs_requirements: URS-EMS-014: System shall interface with existing facility management system via standard protocols
URS-EMS-015: Alarm notifications shall integrate with site paging system using vendor API
URS-EMS-011: System response time shall not exceed 30 seconds for alarm conditions

test_cases.test_name: Audit Trail and Electronic Signature Functionality Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that the system maintains a compliant audit trail and electronic signature functionality as per regulatory requirements
prerequisites: EMS system operational with audit trail feature enabled
User accounts with different privilege levels configured
Test data available for electronic signature testing
System clock synchronized to correct time

test_steps.action: Perform various system actions including data entry, modification, and deletion
test_steps.expected_result: All actions are recorded in the audit trail with timestamp and user identification

test_steps.action: Apply electronic signature to a critical record using vendor's built-in functionality
test_steps.expected_result: Signature is applied successfully with proper attribution and timestamp

test_steps.action: Verify audit trail entries cannot be modified or deleted by any user
test_steps.expected_result: Audit trail records are read-only and protected from modification

test_steps.action: Generate audit trail report using vendor's standard reporting feature
test_steps.expected_result: Report includes all required elements with proper formatting and completeness

acceptance_criteria: All system actions are recorded in the audit trail with complete information
Electronic signatures function correctly using vendor's built-in functionality
Audit trail records are secure and cannot be altered or deleted
System complies with 21 CFR Part 11 requirements for electronic records
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records and signatures
EU Annex 11 requirements for audit trails
FDA guidance on electronic record keeping
data_integrity_requirements: Audit trail must capture all critical data changes
Electronic signatures must be uniquely linked to respective records
Audit records must be time-stamped and sequential
Data must be protected from unauthorized modification
urs_requirements: URS-EMS-008: System shall maintain an audit trail per 21 CFR Part 11
URS-EMS-009: Electronic signatures shall use vendor's built-in functionality
URS-EMS-010: Data shall be retained for 7 years using vendor's archival feature

test_cases.test_name: System Availability and Uptime Performance Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify the system meets the 99.5% availability requirement excluding planned maintenance periods

test_steps.action: Deploy system uptime monitoring software to track EMS availability continuously for 30 days
test_steps.expected_result: Uptime monitoring software successfully installed and configured to track EMS system status

test_steps.action: Record all planned maintenance activities during the 30-day monitoring period
test_steps.expected_result: Complete log of all planned maintenance activities with start/end times maintained

test_steps.action: Calculate system availability percentage excluding planned maintenance time after 30 days
test_steps.expected_result: Availability percentage calculated accurately using total time minus planned maintenance downtime

acceptance_criteria: System availability equals or exceeds 99.5% excluding planned maintenance time
All unplanned downtime events are documented with root cause analysis
regulatory_basis: GMP requirements for continuous monitoring systems
Quality system availability expectations
data_integrity_requirements: Uptime data must be complete and accurate
Time stamps must be synchronized and reliable
All downtime events must be properly documented
urs_requirements: URS-EMS-013: System availability shall be 99.5% excluding planned maintenance
related_tests: OQ-001: Temperature Monitoring Accuracy and Alarm Functionality Verification

test_cases.test_name: Vendor Standard Report Functionality and Batch Release Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that vendor-provided standard reports function correctly and meet batch release requirements
prerequisites: User accounts with appropriate permissions configured
Sample batch data available in system

test_steps.action: Access the vendor's standard report menu and select the batch release report template
test_steps.expected_result: Batch release report template is available and accessible from the standard report menu

test_steps.action: Generate a batch release report for a specific time period covering a complete storage cycle
test_steps.expected_result: Report generates successfully with all required data fields populated

test_steps.action: Verify report contains all required elements: temperature data, time stamps, alarm events, and compliance status
test_steps.expected_result: Report includes all mandatory data elements as specified in URS and regulatory requirements

test_steps.action: Validate that the report can be exported to required formats and includes electronic signature capability
test_steps.expected_result: Report exports successfully to required formats and electronic signature functionality works as intended

acceptance_criteria: All vendor standard reports generate without errors
Batch release reports contain all required compliance data
Reports support electronic signatures per 21 CFR Part 11
Export functionality works for all required formats
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements
GMP batch release documentation requirements
Data integrity ALCOA+ principles
data_integrity_requirements: Reports must accurately reflect source data without modification
Electronic signatures must be securely applied and verifiable
Report data must be complete and unaltered
urs_requirements: URS-EMS-007: Standard reports provided by vendor shall be used for batch release
URS-EMS-009: Electronic signatures shall use vendor's built-in functionality
related_tests: OQ-004: Audit Trail and Electronic Signature Functionality Verification

test_cases.test_name: Vendor Standard Database Format and Data Storage Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that the EMS stores all monitoring data in the vendor's standard database format without modification and ensures data integrity.

test_steps.action: Access the EMS database using vendor-provided tools or credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: Successful connection to the database with appropriate access rights.

test_steps.action: Generate temperature data by exposing probes to known temperature conditions for 1 hour.
test_steps.expected_result: Temperature readings are recorded at 5-minute intervals as specified.

test_steps.action: Query the database to retrieve the stored temperature data and verify the storage format.
test_steps.expected_result: All data is stored in vendor's standard database format without modification.

test_steps.action: Attempt to modify stored data directly through database interface.
test_steps.expected_result: System prevents direct modification of stored monitoring data.

acceptance_criteria: All temperature data stored in vendor standard database format
Data recording intervals do not exceed 5 minutes
Direct database modifications are prevented
Data integrity maintained throughout storage process
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 compliance for electronic records
GMP data integrity requirements
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be stored in original vendor format without modification
Prevention of unauthorized data alteration
Maintenance of complete data chain

test_cases.test_name: System Interface and Protocol Compatibility Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that the EMS properly interfaces with the facility management system using standard protocols and integrates with site paging system.
prerequisites: Site paging system configured for testing

test_steps.action: Configure EMS to communicate with the facility management system using standard protocols (e.g., Modbus, OPC).
test_steps.expected_result: Successful configuration and connection establishment between systems.

test_steps.action: Simulate temperature alarm condition to trigger interface communication.
test_steps.expected_result: EMS successfully transmits alarm data to facility management system.
data_to_capture: Alarm data received by facility system

test_steps.action: Configure EMS to integrate with site paging system using vendor API.
test_steps.expected_result: Successful configuration of paging system integration.

test_steps.action: Trigger alarm condition and verify paging system notification.
test_steps.expected_result: Alarm notification is successfully sent to site paging system within specified response time.

acceptance_criteria: EMS interfaces successfully with facility management system using standard protocols
Alarm data transmitted accurately and completely
Paging system integration functions properly
Response time meets 30-second requirement for alarm conditions
regulatory_basis: GMP requirements for integrated monitoring systems
21 CFR Part 11 for electronic data exchange
data_integrity_requirements: Accurate data transmission between systems
Maintenance of data integrity during interface operations
Secure communication protocols

test_cases.test_name: Vendor Standard Software Configuration and Unmodified Deployment Verification
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS software is installed using the vendor's standard, unmodified installation package and that all default configurations are validated for GMP use.
prerequisites: Target server/workstation meets vendor-specified hardware requirements

test_steps.action: Execute the vendor-provided installation package on the designated server/workstation.
test_steps.expected_result: Installation wizard launches successfully without errors and proceeds to the configuration screen.

test_steps.action: Complete the installation using all default settings and configurations as specified by the vendor.
test_steps.expected_result: Software installs completely without requiring any custom code or configuration modifications.
data_to_capture: List of installed components from the log

test_steps.action: Verify the installed software version and checksum against the vendor's release documentation.
test_steps.expected_result: Installed version matches the vendor's validated release, and file checksums confirm no modifications.

acceptance_criteria: Software installs successfully using vendor defaults only
No custom code or configuration modifications are required
Installed version matches the vendor's validated release documentation
regulatory_basis: GAMP 5 Guide: Category 3 - Standard Software
FDA guidance on use of off-the-shelf software in regulated environments
data_integrity_requirements: Installation logs must be retained as part of system documentation
Software version integrity must be verified against vendor source

test_cases.test_name: Continuous Monitoring Interval and Data Recording Verification
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system continuously monitors and records temperature data at the required maximum 5-minute intervals without data loss.
prerequisites: EMS software is successfully installed and operational
At least one temperature probe is connected and calibrated
System clock is synchronized to official time source

test_steps.action: Configure the system to monitor a connected temperature probe with a 5-minute recording interval as specified in URS-EMS-002.
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts the configuration and displays the 5-minute interval setting as active.

test_steps.action: Monitor the system for a period of 30 minutes (6 expected data points) and verify data recording.
test_steps.expected_result: System records temperature readings at exactly 5-minute intervals, generating 6 consecutive data points.
data_to_capture: Timestamp of each recorded data point

test_steps.action: Verify that all recorded data points are stored in the vendor's standard database and are accessible for reporting.
test_steps.expected_result: All 6 data points are present in the database and can be retrieved through standard queries.
data_to_capture: Database query results showing all data points
Screenshot of data retrieval from reporting interface

acceptance_criteria: System records temperature data at intervals not exceeding 5 minutes
No data gaps or missing recordings during the test period
All data is properly stored in the vendor's standard database format
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 11: Clause 12 - Data Storage
21 CFR Part 211.68 - Automatic mechanical and electronic equipment
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be recorded with accurate timestamps
Complete data sequence must be maintained without gaps
Data must be protected from unauthorized modification
